 Lewis Hamilton calls on Israel to open Gaza aid routes after Rafah border visit
 November 17, 2026 
 Shares Following a trip to the Rafah border crossing earlier this week, seven-time Formula 1 world champion Lewis Hamilton has demanded that Israel allow humanitarian relief trucks to enter Gaza, condemning the ongoing crisis in stark terms.
 The Ferrari driver, who previously advocated for a ceasefire and expressed support for a “Free Palestine” before October’s United States Grand Prix, traveled to Rafah, the only land entry point connecting Egypt and the Gaza Strip and a central staging area for global relief agencies.
 After speaking directly with truck drivers and humanitarian staff on site, Hamilton addressed his 44 million Instagram followers with a detailed account of what he witnessed.
 “The past three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling,” Hamilton wrote. “It’s an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.”
 Israeli officials have repeatedly rejected charges of genocide, stating that their military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas fighters.
 In his statement, Hamilton urged the public not to grow numb to the humanitarian toll. “I know so many people that feel that same helplessness,” he wrote. “That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don’t want us to get used to their suffering. I don’t want us to look away.”
 While in Egypt, Hamilton also conferred with North Sinai Governor Khaled Megawer. Footage posted to the governor’s official Facebook page showed Megawer outlining regional relief logistics for the British driver, who also greeted aid workers and asked about how frequently supply convoys are permitted across the border.
 Hamilton highlighted severe delays holding up essential cargo, echoing a warning issued last month by the World Health Organization (WHO) that prolonged holdups of prosthetics and critical medical supplies could lead to “devastating consequences” for Palestinians.
 “I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help,” Hamilton posted. “At the Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they’re regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours. At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids. Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.”
 Formula 1 drops Imola contingency plan ahead of  West Asia finale
 Hamilton’s visit coincides with Formula 1 finalizing its plans to wrap up the 2026 season in West Asia. This week, series officials notified Italy’s Imola circuit that it will not be needed to host a backup finale on December 6, confirming that the championship will conclude with a triple-header in Las Vegas (November 21), Qatar (November 29), and Abu Dhabi (December 6).
 Regional instability earlier in 2026 forced Formula 1 to scrap April events in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, though Bahrain later financed a replacement race in Malaysia in October. F1 had kept Imola on standby in case fighting escalated after the U.S. midterm elections, despite the Italian venue having already begun erecting grandstands. Officials gained confidence to proceed with the original calendar after MotoGP, which is also owned by Liberty Media, completed a race weekend in Qatar last week without disruption.
 While none of the 11 F1 teams face corporate travel bans preventing them from competing in Qatar or Abu Dhabi, the final two rounds could still be called off if hostilities flare up again. Without Imola as a fallback, canceling those races would end the season in Las Vegas and leave the 2026 schedule at 21 Grands Prix, one short of the 22-race minimum required under Formula 1’s commercial agreements with the teams.
 Both 2026 championships have already been clinched, with Kimi Antonelli sealing the drivers’ title in Mexico and Mercedes locking up the constructors’ trophy in Brazil, leaving mid-grid teams to battle over remaining prize money positions in the final rounds.
